newsitem.title: UK: NORTH SEA MARKETS QUIET, CFDS WELL OFFERED.
newsitem.headline: NORTH SEA MARKETS QUIET, CFDS WELL OFFERED.

text.p: Little early action was seen on the North Sea market with refiners and traders alike waiting for the September crude loading programes due out later on Wednesday and tomorrow, traders said.
The September Ekofisk programme was unsurprising at 39 cargoes.
"Just as expected - right on the button," one trader said.
September IPE Brent lost 11 cents to $18.73 a barrel in very thin early trade.
Overnight API statistics showed a crude build of over 2.7 million barrels where a draw had been expected, but traders said they saw some product support from reduced U.S. refinery utilisation.
News of an August 26-28 Statfjord deal done late on Tuesday at Dated Brent +25 cents confirmed that there was some strength in the few remaining barrels.
That was the last remaining August loading Statfjord and only one or possibly two Ekofisks were left, traders said.
There were three Brent crude cargoes passing through the paper chains on Wednesday.
Talk was steady around September -25/-15 cents.

CFD markets were quiet and well offered. Next week and the following three weeks were heard offered around October -23/22 cents. Brent Sept/Oct was -12/-10 cents with Oct/Nov -14/-10 cents. The Brent Sept/Oct traded three times, twice at -11 cents and once at -10 cents.
